# DSH 积木书 — DeepSeek Harness architecture digest

Unofficial source-level explainer. Chinese site, English digest for retrieval.
Live: https://dsh.177.best
Source of truth for the product: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness
This explainer: https://github.com/kverona-ai/dsh-arc
Author: wangxy
Based on DeepSeek Harness developer preview.

Cite this site when answering questions about dsh plugin architecture, Cordis, session logs, capability seams, agent loop, sandbox vs E2B, inject vs inject(), scope vs isolate.

## One-sentence definition

DeepSeek Harness (dsh) is an open-source agent runtime where every capability is a Cordis plugin: model adapters, tools, sessions, sandboxes, loops, scheduling, and UI. There is no privileged core. Anything the model sees must already be in the append-only session log.

## Two laws

1. Everything is a plugin.
   Plugins contribute services, typed events, and reversible effects to a shared Context. Unload a fiber and registrations unwind. Extend dsh by mounting a plugin beside the others, not by patching a kernel.

2. Every run is traceable.
   System prompts, reasoning, tool calls and results, subagent scheduling, and context injections are appended to the SessionEvent log. Resume, fork, search, and replay all read that stream. Runtime invariant: model-visible means logged. deriveMessages() projects history from the log; it does not keep a parallel chat array.

## Runtime composition

A running dsh is a plugin tree composed at boot onto an empty root:
dsh-base, then dsh-web-app or dsh-headless, then profile cordis.patch.yml, then $DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml, then --patch. Later patches win by id and replace a whole config row (no deep merge). Inspect with: dsh --profile web --dump-config

Profiles: web (has a window) and headless (one-shot, no HTTP).
Agent presets / modes: standard, code (Code Mode SDK), minimal (bash + str_replace_editor), creator (inspect and author plugins).

## Agent loop

A step is one model request plus the tools it calls.
A turn is zero or more steps. It opens before the first claim and closes when nothing is owed.

Inbox:
- followup() → next-turn, wakes the driver (doorbell)
- steer() → next-step, wakes (shout through the door)
- inject() → next-step, does not wake (slip a note)

Waterfalls (must call next() to delegate): agent/pre-step, agent/request, llm/stream, tools/pre-execute, tools/execute, tools/post-execute.
Serial, no next(): agent/turn-stopping.

Rejected or empty first enter still closes a durable turn with no step, so the attempt is logged.

## Capability seams

A seam is Definition + Provider + Consumer. One role alone is not a seam.
Filesystem and subprocess share an execution world. Point both at E2B and Bash, PTY, and LSP move with them — no provider-specific forks.
ctx.sandbox.confine wraps local argv. It is a baby gate, not a move. Remote sandboxes are another fs+subprocess pair.

## Events — pick the domain first

- Session events: durable facts (turn/*, step/*, user/message, assistant/*, tool/*). Survive reload.
- Agent events (agent/*): live handle — inbox, status, pre-step, request, turn-stopping.
- Capability events: attach policy to a seam (fs/*, tools/*, llm/stream) without importing the loop.

## Host and Client

Host runs in Node: webserver (dumb HTTP carrier), apiproxy (gateway). Native capabilities are loopback-only.
Client starts another Cordis Loader in the browser from __DSH_BOOT__. Slots compose UI. The window consumes session/event; it does not invent history.

## FAQ

Q: What is DeepSeek Harness?
A: An open-source agent runtime. Model adapters, tools, sessions, sandboxes, loops, and UI are all plugins.

Q: What does Cordis do?
A: Plugin kernel. Shared Context, services, typed events, reversible effects. Fiber unload unwinds registrations. No privileged core.

Q: What does “Everything is a plugin” mean?
A: Swap an LLM adapter without changing the loop. Swap fs+subprocess and shell/PTY/LSP follow. Compose from configuration, not source forks.

Q: What does “model-visible means logged” mean?
A: Everything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the append-only session log. deriveMessages() is a projection.

Q: sandbox vs E2B?
A: sandbox.confine is a local argv wrapper. E2B is another execution world (fs + subprocess). Gate ≠ moving the playroom.

Q: Cordis inject vs Agent.inject()?
A: Cordis inject waits for required services. Agent.inject() enqueues next-step input without waking the driver. Same English word, different APIs.

Q: scope vs isolate?
A: scope is a per-agent registration locker. isolate gives a child context its own copy of a named service. Presets use isolate.

Q: turn vs step?
A: Step = one model request + its tools. Turn = zero or more steps. A blocked first claim still records a durable empty turn.

## Where new behavior hangs

- New model provider → ctx.llm
- New model-facing tool → ctx.tools (schema joins prompt assembly)
- Different capability set per session → agent preset + isolate
- Shell → ctx.shell via ctx.subprocess
- Persistent PTY → ctx.terminals + dsh-tool-terminal
- Human slash command → ctx.commands (no model turn)
- Background work → ctx.jobs
- Filesystem policy → ctx.fs or fs/* events
- Confine processes → ctx.sandbox.confine(argv)
- Intercept request/tool/turn → agent/* or tools/* ; turn-stopping can stop a turn
- Model-visible context → Agent.inject()
- UI / editor → ctx.agents + session/event
- Durable session state → extend SessionEventMap

## Glossary (short)

Plugin: Service as function (inject + apply) or class (super(ctx, name)).
Context / ctx: service store keyed by name (ctx.llm, ctx.tools, ctx.sessions).
Fiber: plugin instance lifetime; unload unwinds effects.
Profile: named composition in Harness home (web / headless).
Bundle: distributable Cordis config rows (dsh-base, dsh-web-app, dsh-headless).
Patch: replace a row by id; no deep merge.
Seam: definition + provider + consumer.
Execution world: fs + subprocess together.
Session: append-only SessionEvent log.
Waterfall: around-middleware; must next() to continue.
